title: Minimax Recovery of Exact Initiation-Time Risk in Randomized Scheduling Experiments
banked_reason: Randomized assignment of initiation time does not by construction make the postinitiation terminal hazard invariant to assigned time or treatment duration; the proposal expressly disclaims ordinary scheduling applicability and supplies no realistic regime in which this load-bearing exclusion is credible.
gap_reasons: Exact equality of the entire post-initiation hazard surface across an open timing band is a load-bearing and substantially stronger condition than ordinary local regularity, while the protocol-band sentence gives no concrete setting or evidence in which it is credible.

Randomized assignment of initiation time does not by construction make the postinitiation terminal hazard invariant to assigned time or treatment duration; the proposal expressly disclaims ordinary scheduling applicability and supplies no realistic regime in which this load-bearing exclusion is credible.
proof_attempt_summary: Four D-0.5 revisions repaired the observed-law exposure definition, causal-law domains, and finite-sample positivity, then narrowed the claim to an explicit randomized-scheduling calibration experiment. The reviewer still found the flat postinitiation hazard assumption unsupported as an applicable causal regime; the independent validity gate confirmed that relaxing it changes the first-order Gaussian game and requires a new topic. No D0 derivation or Lean formalization was launched; the scalar decision-theory presolve remains unverified downstream.
tldr: Exact assigned initiation is studied as a canonical nonregular target in a mathematical randomized-scheduling calibration experiment. Eligible subjects receive an assigned time with positive density in a fixed interior band, and the postinitiation terminal intensity is, by construction, \(Y_1(r)a(r)\), independent of assigned time and treatment duration in that band, with measurable \(a\) bounded away from zero and infinity on \([u_{\star}-\eta_0,t]\). This restriction implies identifiable mean-zero scheduling contrasts and is rejected by their population failure; nonrejection does not establish exact equality. The observed information is the constrained symmetric density section \(R(r)=\rho(r,u_{\star})\) of \(\mu_r(B)=E_0\{Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_1(r)\mathbf 1(U\in B)\}\), with \(q=R/a\) and \(J=\int q^{-1/2}\). The project reduces the resulting game to scalar Lipschitz white noise, certifies unrestricted squared-risk and \(90\%\)-honest connected-interval values, proves strict affine-benchmark improvements, and transfers the decisions under conditional censoring, delayed entry, measurable event-time hazards, and the iterated order \(n\to\infty\) through \(n\ge N_H\) followed by \(H\to\infty\).
gap: Published causal survival inference replaces exact initiation by a positive-width intervention because the exact-time risk is not pathwise differentiable. Gaussian optimal-recovery papers provide affine or near-minimax benchmarks, and censored-survival learning papers provide regular limits, but no source certifies unrestricted exact-time decision values and observed-data attainment in a randomized-scheduling calibration experiment.
fill: A predictable exposure lemma derives measurability and positive essential bounds for the identical \(q=R/a\) from the explicit measures \(\nu_0\) and \(\nu_{n,h}\). The full-band lower hazard bound and the Lipschitz-support envelope give the explicit validity threshold \(N_H=\max\{1,\lceil(LH/a_{\min})^3\rceil,\lceil(H/\eta_0)^3\rceil\}\). A rank-one lower subexperiment and matching projection identify both values through \(J\); certified games and finite-vector martingale expansions use this same information version for lower bounds, learning, risk, coverage, and the exact iterated expected-length criterion.
